In a lengthy interview with Joanna Stern, OpenAI president Greg Brockman responded to the company's recent changes to the ChatGPT desktop app and discussed their plans for a tabless interface. Watch the video below.

The Work functionality will soon be seamlessly integrated into ChatGPT

A few days ago, Joanna Stern uploaded a preview clip of her interview with OpenAI president Greg Brockman on her new YouTube channel, New Things.

Stern has today released the full interview, covering a range of topics including the new ChatGPT voice features, OpenAI's hardware ambitions, the lawsuit against Apple, and the recent Hugging Face data leak.

During the interview, Stern noted OpenAI's recent decision to merge the ChatGPT and Codex desktop apps and roll out a new agentic Work mode for ChatGPT.

The result was a chaotic interface, especially for users who wanted to keep using ChatGPT but couldn't find their chat history no matter what they did.

OpenAI subsequently updated the app, re-adding separate Work and Chat tabs at the top and a dropdown menu in the sidebar to let users switch between ChatGPT and Codex. While the app isn't as hard to use as before, it still feels a bit roundabout in practice.

Asked about the misstep, Brockman agreed with Stern, conceding that the new interface was "a bit messy," but added that it was a "stepping stone toward the future," and mentioned that the Work tab would eventually disappear, with its functionality being "seamlessly woven into ChatGPT."

Below is Brockman's full response:

Brockman also said that, despite the confusing rollout of the merged app, OpenAI had already seen the intended effect: in just a few days, Codex users had doubled from 5 million to 10 million.

When Stern pressed him on whether that growth was simply the result of shoving Codex into the ChatGPT app, Brockman once again conceded that was indeed the case, while also arguing that it was partly the point:

The full interview is quite interesting and well worth a watch. It also features a very "Joanna Stern-style" attempt at bringing ChatGPT's voice features into the conversation, with results pretty much as everyone expected.
